service_image: built from the service code at dev c45c573 (the commit before the deploy tooling), ARM64

instance.service: ECS Express Mode, Fargate ARM64, 0.5 vCPU, 1 GB, exactly one task
instance.database: Aurora Serverless v2, PostgreSQL 16.15, minimum 0, maximum 1 unit (one run at 4), private subnets, TLS required
instance.load_balancer: ECS Express Mode application load balancer, shared with the live service

dataset: a clean copy: a second database inside the same cluster, seeded with the 4-stage chain and 10 sources; k6 builds chains of depth 8 and 12 (the cap) in setup; no live data touched
limits_used: per-address and global publish limits, report and ingest limits, the storage threshold and the per-stage fork limit were LIFTED on the copy so a single client would measure the service and not the limiter; everything else as deployed; uploads off
client: k6 1.0.0 (pinned image) on a laptop over a home connection, one client address; latencies include that network path

smoke.profile: smoke: 8 s per scenario, a check that the script works

full.profile: full: 60 s per scenario; 60 reads/s, 6 flips/s (two scenarios), 60 mixed/s (20% flips), a ramp to 12 flips/s

stress_1_unit.profile: stress: 250 reads/s, 20 flips/s, 250 mixed/s, a ramp to 80 flips/s

stress_4_units.profile: the same stress, database maximum raised to 4 units for this run only

stress_1_unit.database: capacity pinned at its 1.0-unit maximum and database CPU 100% for the whole run

stress_4_units.note: the 5xx are the service's named 503 retry-later refusals, counted by k6 as polite refusals, not errors

not_covered: no cold database: the database was awake throughout
no sustained hours: the longest run is about 5 minutes
no real mobile network and no browser: only the service HTTP interface
the live service shared the database's capacity during these runs
no claim about a number of users: none is extrapolated
